clue.text: Miss clamour about extreme characters in musical

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the outcry wraps the letters that follow

parts.note: to clamour is to cry out
A and Z are the characters at the two extremes of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A young woman shouts about the ends of the alphabet in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl Crazy is a 1930 Gershwin musical; 'Miss' looks like a verb, failing to hit, but is a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Girl Crazy is a Gershwin stage show from 1930, so it is an example of a musical.

clue.text: Ugly garden ornament's not new: regrets replacing it

indicators.note: not new says the letter for new, N, has to go from the ornament
replacing it says the regrets go in where that dropped letter for new stood

parts.note: a gnome is a little figure standing in a garden as an ornament
to regret is to rue, so regrets gives rues

explanation.surface: Someone finds a garden gnome hideous and rues buying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not new' drops N from GNOME and 'replacing it' puts RUES in that gap: G + RUES + OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome is horrible to look at, a stronger synonym of ugly.

clue.text: French writer losing head creates stir

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the writer's name is dropped

parts.note: Marcel Proust was the French novelist of In Search of Lost Time

explanation.surface: A French author's decapitation causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops P from PROUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to stir someone up or rouse them out of bed, so it is a synonym of stir.

clue.text: Holiday changes occur at home without me

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words that follow are rearranged
without says the letters of me are taken out of that pool before the rest is rearranged

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday plan shifts so that something happens at home, but not to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: OCCURATHOME less M and E leaves CCURATHOO, which 'changes' rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach tour is a holiday travelling from place to place by bus.

clue.text: A king, then another, appearing in a couple of grand drawings

parts.note: taken as written
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: appearing in says the second king goes inside the couple of grand

parts.note: a couple is two and a grand is K, a thousand, so two K
another king, so a second R

explanation.surface: Two kings feature in a pair of fine sketches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' puts the second R inside TWOK, giving TWORK after A and R. K for a thousand comes from kilo.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork is the illustrative matter in a publication, a collective term covering drawings.

clue.text: Unknown variety of premium drops soft, with better flavour

parts.note: in algebra y is an unknown quantity

indicators.note: variety of says the letters of the next word come in a different order
drops says one letter is taken out of the word premium

parts.note: the word supplies the letters to rearrange
p, for piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A new premium blend drops some of its smoothness but tastes better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges what is left once 'drops' removes P from the fodder. 'drops' is a verb here, not liquid drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Yummier is the comparative of yummy, meaning tastier, so it means having a better flavour.

clue.text: Footwear this old would get ruined

definitions.text: Footwear this old would get ruined

parts.words: Footwear this old would get ruined
parts.note: a wooden clog with age added after it becomes a word for deliberate wrecking, said to come from workers throwing clogs into machines

explanation.surface: Old shoes like these would be falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Add AGE ('old') to the answer and you get SABOTAGE, deliberate ruin. The OCR added ES to the clue from the page margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog worn by French peasants, a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Boots out, on reflection, for character's small foot

indicators.note: on reflection says the word is mirrored, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: to boot out is to sack, and to sack is to fire, so boots out gives fires

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, a manager sacks someone for the sake of a small detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns FIRES backwards. 'Boots' looks like footwear, matching 'foot', but means sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the short stroke at the end of a letter's line, the small foot of a printed character.

clue.text: At the end of the Archers, person dropping off heavy tractor

parts.words: At the end of the Archers
parts.note: the bull is the target at the far end of an archery range that archers aim for
someone dropping off to sleep is a dozer

explanation.surface: At the close of the radio soap The Archers, a listener nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set on farms; the clue reads like a listener sleeping through it, but the bull is the archers' target.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulldozer is a heavy tracked tractor with a blade for pushing earth.

clue.text: Casually proceed to call from Madrid? About time!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: About says the cry is wrapped round the letter for time

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of approval heard in Madrid

explanation.surface: A Spanish shout urging someone to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: Ole is the cheer of a Spanish bullfight crowd; 'About' wraps it round T, and the exclamation 'About time!' hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: To tootle is to drive or walk along in a leisurely way, so it means proceed casually.

clue.text: Sort of radiation, nuclear, regularly causing flap

parts.note: UV is ultraviolet, a kind of radiation

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Ultraviolet and nuclear radiation cause some kind of flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of nuclear: U, L, A.
explanation.definitionFit: The uvula is the fleshy flap hanging at the back of the soft palate.

clue.text: In Sri Lankan area, run and look for fruit

indicators.note: In says the next pieces go inside the Sri Lankan

parts.note: a Tamil is one of a people of Sri Lanka
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Someone in a part of Sri Lanka runs about searching for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sets A and R inside the Sri Lankan; LO, as in 'lo and behold', is a crossword staple for look.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarillo is the egg-shaped tree tomato, an edible fruit.

clue.text: Jazz musician makes church tick on one day of the week

indicators.note: on says the church and tick are put after the day

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
a tick is a moment, shortened to mo

explanation.surface: A musician arranges a church service for a particular weekday.
explanation.walkthrough: Satchmo was the nickname of the trumpeter Louis Armstrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchmo was the nickname of Louis Armstrong, the trumpeter and singer, so he is a jazz musician.

clue.text: Pagan chessmen: one knight left out

indicators.note: out here means on the outside, so these letters go round the chess body

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the chess notation for knight
FIDE is the world chess federation, the body of chess players

explanation.surface: An irreligious chess set loses a knight from its pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts I, N and L outside FIDE: IN + FIDE + L. The surface makes chessmen the pieces on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is one without the true faith, a synonym of pagan.

clue.text: Chap interferes, say, engaging one putting aside literary award

indicators.note: engaging means holding within, so the reserver sits between the two pieces

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to interfere or pry gives pries
a booker is one who reserves or puts something aside

explanation.surface: A man meddles, enlisting someone who sets things aside, over a literary prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you the meddling word is heard as the award noun; 'engaging' sets the reserver between the chap and that noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Man Booker Prize was the name of the Booker Prize for fiction from 2002 to 2019, a literary award.

clue.text: Want to eat seconds — seen going up to collect these

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so the turned word holds the other pieces
in a down clue going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to dine is to eat
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Wanting a second helping, as seen in those who come up for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns the seen word upside down in the column, and 'collect' takes the eating and S inside it. 'these' just refers back to the seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is a state of poverty or lack, a synonym of want as a noun.

clue.text: Checkpoint board arranged with added security feature

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of board are put in a new order

parts.note: a lock is a security feature added to a door

explanation.surface: A board is put up with an extra lock as a security measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns BOARD into ROADB.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadblock is a barrier where traffic is stopped and checked, a checkpoint.

clue.text: What sounds unhealthy passion for tree

indicators.note: What sounds says the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: sick means unhealthy or ill; amour is French for love, a passion

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what name sounds like a sickly love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, sick amour matches the name of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple, a common tree in Britain.

clue.text: The host baked a carrot tart: my energy's restored!

indicators.note: baked says the letters are cooked up into something new

parts.note: the words supply most of the letters to rearrange
taken as written
E, the abbreviation for energy, is put back into the mix

explanation.surface: Someone bakes a carrot tart and finds their energy returning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' rearranges the tart and MY with E, the energy that is 'restored' to the pool. 'The host' looks like a dinner host, but it means a great army.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is an army or great multitude, and the Terracotta Army is a host of clay soldiers.

clue.text: Amusing partner in surgery?

parts.note: co- means joint or partner, as in co-pilot
a medic is one who works in a surgery, the British word for a doctor's office

explanation.surface: A joke about an assistant in an operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as CO-MEDIC, a fellow doctor. In Britain a surgery is a doctor's consulting room.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic means relating to comedy, so it means amusing.

clue.text: Cock that's heading west, confused

indicators.note: heading says the first letter of that's is taken

parts.note: addle means muddled or confused

explanation.surface: A rooster is heading west, bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang cock means nonsense, as in a load of cock, not a rooster.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle is silly talk, and cock is British slang for the same nonsense.

clue.text: Olde-worlde set of books briefly, fearfully, turn back covers

indicators.note: in a down clue covers says one piece sits on top of the other
briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to quail is to shrink back in fear
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned set of books whose covers are turned back in fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops L from QUAIL; in a down answer 'covers' puts QUAI above NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means attractively old-fashioned, which olde-worlde mockingly says.

clue.text: Flat found east of Oxford, perhaps

indicators.note: east of says this piece goes to the right of the other

parts.note: Oxford is an example of a university, shortened to uni
to found is to form or set up

explanation.surface: An apartment found to the east of Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' is the adjective meaning even, not a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means flat in the sense of even and unvarying throughout.

clue.text: Last thing in the evening finally visiting old, old woman

indicators.note: visiting says the letters go inside the old woman

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old woman in slang

indicators.note: finally says the last letter of each of the words the and evening is taken

explanation.surface: Late at night someone finally calls on an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and G, which 'visiting' puts inside MA after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is the last thing.

clue.text: Bachelor not sleeping around coming to a province

indicators.note: around says the wakeful word is put round the bachelor

parts.note: alert means wide awake, not sleeping

explanation.surface: A single man who cannot sleep comes to a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts B inside ALERT, giving ALBERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is a province of western Canada.

clue.text: Old-style concierge picked up where principal left off

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means the word is lifted to read from bottom to top
the principal, first, letter of the concierge is left off

parts.note: a porter is a doorkeeper, as a concierge is

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned doorman takes over after the headteacher stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop P from PORTER to leave ORTER; 'picked up' turns it backwards. 'picked up' is not a sound signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro means imitating styles of the past, so it means old-style.

clue.text: Series of fine Verdi duets that amazes me

indicators.note: Series of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An opera fan is astonished at a run of fine Verdi duets.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from fINE through VERDI to DUets.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in astonishment, the phrase is an exclamation of surprise: well, that amazes me.

clue.text: Upmarket Irish politician in pair of spectacles and cap

indicators.note: in says the posh letter and the politician go inside the spectacles

parts.note: two Os look like a pair of glasses
U means upper-class, upmarket
a TD, Teachta Dala, is a member of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: A posh Irish politician wears glasses and a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the posh letter and the Irish MP between the two lenses. 'cap' is the verb meaning surpass, not a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to better it, so it means to outdo.

clue.text: Unit working least

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A team that works the least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: The tesla is the SI unit of magnetic flux density.

clue.text: Employing effrontery and aplomb, finally I face constituent

parts.note: cheek is impudence, effrontery

indicators.note: finally says the last letter of aplomb is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: With nerve and poise, someone finally faces up to a voter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituent' looks like a voter but means a component part.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheekbone is the bone below the eye, part of the face.
